title: Wizard: detect a migration alias collision from the preview and offer the fix before applying
description:
Follow-up to LCLI-465 (which exposed --preserve-source-ids/--source-family as non-interactive flags). opum-agent's approved item 2: 'Surface the preview's collision rather than a bare exit 5... Prefer asking before applying, over reporting after failing: you have a preview step and an interactive wizard, so you can detect the collision and offer the flags before anything is attempted.'

Today the interactive wizard's migrate choice runs the same migrateBacklogTasksToQuest path LCLI-465 fixed for the flag path, but has no way to retry with --preserve-source-ids/--source-family since the wizard never asks about them -- a wizard user hitting the alias collision still gets a bare exit 5, even though the flag path can now avoid it entirely.

Confirmed via quest-cli: their message fix (QCLI-256) now distinguishes the two collision causes -- positional renumbering (LCLI-465's fix applies) vs. a genuine dual id claim (no automatic fix exists, needs manual resolution). Any wizard-side collision handling must read which cause a refusal names before assuming --preserve-source-ids helps.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The wizard's migrate path runs Quest's preview first (as today) and, on an alias-collision refusal, distinguishes positional-renumbering causes (offer to retry with --preserve-source-ids/--source-family, prompting for the family) from a genuine dual-claim collision (explain that this needs manual resolution, per quest-cli's QCLI-256 message)
A wizard user who accepts the retry offer gets a successful migration without re-running lore init by hand
Verified against a real repro (both collision shapes) in a real terminal, not just unit tests

plan: 1. Repro both collision shapes with the real backlog+quest binaries and read what Quest actually returns
2. Classify the refusal in tracker-migration.ts: an alias-collision refusal names BOTH causes, so the cause is decided by re-running Quest preview in preservation mode, not by parsing prose
3. Wizard: on a collision, offer the preserve-source-ids retry, prompt for the family, re-run; a preservation refusal is reported as needing manual resolution with no retry offered
4. Tests (unit + mutation check) and a real-binary end-to-end repro
implementationNotes: Measured Quest 0.7.1's two refusals against real repros built with backlog 1.50.1 + quest 0.7.1. The DEFAULT-mode refusal does NOT say which cause it hit: a positional-renumbering repro (dotted subtask TASK-1.1 flattening onto TASK-2) and a dual-claim repro (destination already holding TASK-1/TASK-2) returned the SAME sentence, naming both causes ('If this is from positional renumbering ... If instead this exact id is already a live, unrelated claim ...'), with no structured input. So the cause is not machine-readable from that refusal. The only reliable discriminator is Quest's own preservation-mode PREVIEW, which mutates nothing: it either returns a plan (positional renumbering, retry works) or refuses with 'Backlog id preservation refused ... No further flag resolves a remaining id collision here' plus structured input.collisions/unpreservable. The wizard is built on that: offer, ask for the family, re-run preview, and let Quest decide.

Real-terminal verification (AC#3): the real `lore init` wizard from this branch was driven over a real pty (python pty.openpty, readline saw isTTY and rendered its prompts) against three scratch repros with the real backlog/quest binaries. (1) positional-renumbering repro: Quest refused, the wizard printed the refusal, offered the retry, pre-filled the family 'TASK' from the quoted id, and the migration APPLIED in the same run -- exit 0, digest 44932ea0..., .quest/tasks holds TASK-1..TASK-4 (TASK-4 is the flattened TASK-1.1), [tracker] backend = quest, pending record cleared. (2) dual-claim repro: same offer, preservation preview refused, lore reported 'no migration flag resolves it' with the manual-resolution hint, exit 5, no third attempt, destination unchanged and [tracker] unwritten. (3) declining the offer re-raised Quest's own refusal verbatim, exit 5. No human typed the answers; the terminal was a pty, not a person.

Mutation check (three mutants, predicted subsets matched exactly): M1 revert the wizard call site to runBacklogMigration(options) -> 3 red, exactly the retry/family-override/dual-claim wizard tests; the decline and non-collision tests stayed green because the unhandled error still propagates. M2 remove the preservation-refused branch from classifyMigrationCollision -> 4 red: the three classifier cases plus the wizard dual-claim case. M3 make familyHint return undefined -> 3 red: the two wizard cases that depend on the pre-filled family plus the classifier's hint assertion; the 'omitted rather than guessed' case correctly stayed green.

Delivered in PR #137 (https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/pull/137), base dev. CI run 35168954907 (ci.yml, pull_request) on the PR head. Tool versions the proofs resolved: lore 0.7.0 (lore check 0, 80 files), quest 0.7.1, backlog 1.50.1, bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0.

CORRECTION BY THE REVIEWING SESSION: THE CI RUN THIS RECORD FIRST CITED WAS CANCELLED, AND THE MECHANISM THAT PUT IT THERE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX.

The preceding note cited run 35168954907 as the evidence. Re-resolved by head SHA rather than trusted: 35168954907 has head 638209e5 and conclusion CANCELLED. The run that actually proves this work is 35168977253, head 383af2978c5adc6e9c36f2a6cb75e6e1db351564, conclusion SUCCESS, every required require-ci-on-dev context green (docker e2e harness, lint/typecheck/test on ubuntu and windows, Tracker integrity, lore check (docs gate)); the two non-success entries are `main is fast-forward of dev` and `promotion is manual`, both skipped because they do not run on a PR into dev.

THE CITATION INVALIDATED ITSELF, STRUCTURALLY. The fleet rule is to close a task citing the PR number and the CI run id, both knowable before the merge, never the merge SHA. Honouring it here meant writing the run id into the tracker record -- which is a commit -- which moved the PR head -- which gave the PR a NEW run and left the just-written citation pointing at the previous head. That is not carelessness; it is a regress the rule contains: any commit that records a run id changes the head whose run it is recording. The first run was additionally cancelled (superseded by the push), so the record cited a run that never reported a verdict at all.

HOW IT TERMINATES, since "cite the newer run" just moves the problem one commit along. The citation names the run that proves the DELIVERABLE -- here 35168977253 on 383af297, which is the head carrying all of the source, tests and docs. A later tracker-only commit (this correction included) carries its own run, which is verified green at merge time and is gated by the required contexts regardless. So the terminating rule is: cite the run that validated the code, state which commit it covers, and let the merge gate cover the citation commits that follow. A reader chasing the cited id should find the run that tested the implementation, not the run that tested the sentence they are reading.

WORTH GENERALISING: this will recur for every task closed under the cite-before-merge rule whenever the close is its own commit, which is the normal case. The reusable form is "name the commit the run covers", not "name the newest run".

AC#3 IS CHECKED, AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT COVER -- recorded so the caveat is on the task rather than only in an implementation session that no longer exists.

WHAT AC#3 ASKS: "Verified against a real repro (both collision shapes) in a real terminal, not just unit tests."

WHAT WAS DONE: both collision shapes were built with the REAL backlog 1.50.1 and quest 0.7.1 binaries in scratch directories, and the real `lore init` wizard from this branch was driven over a REAL PTY (pty.openpty) -- readline saw isTTY true and rendered its own prompts. No prompter double, no injected seam. Repro 1 (positional renumbering: TASK-1, TASK-1.1, TASK-2, TASK-3): offer accepted, family pre-filled TASK from the quoted id, migration applied IN THE SAME RUN, exit 0, digest 44932ea0..., .quest/tasks holding TASK-1..TASK-4 with TASK-4 the flattened TASK-1.1, backend pinned to quest, pending record cleared. Repro 2 (genuine dual claim: destination already holding TASK-1/TASK-2): offer accepted, preservation preview refused, diagnostic raised, exit 5, NO third attempt, destination unchanged and [tracker] unwritten. Decline path: Quest's own refusal re-raised verbatim, exit 5.

WHY THAT SATISFIES THE CRITERION: the risk AC#3 exists to retire is "proven only against a test double". A pty is a real terminal device and the binaries were real, so that risk is retired. The criterion contrasts a real terminal with unit tests, and this is on the real-terminal side of that line.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY HAS TO REDISCOVER IT: no human typed the answers, and the @clack/prompts multiselect step was NOT exercised -- PATH was constrained so no agent binaries were detected and the bridge question was skipped. So the pty runs never crossed clack's raw-mode handoff before reaching the migration.

WHY THAT GAP IS JUDGED NON-BLOCKING RATHER THAN WAVED THROUGH. The retry prompt fires after runInteractiveWizard's try/finally has already closed the prompter, so it depends on createRealPrompter re-opening readline on demand. That was verified two ways, not assumed: in the source, openReadline() explicitly recreates the interface when alreadyClosed is set -- machinery LCLI-462 added for precisely the multiselect close/reopen cycle -- and empirically, the pty runs exercised a prompt after that close and it worked. A run WITH agents detected would take the same openReadline() path, one cycle earlier. The combination is untested; the mechanism it depends on is not.

IF A LATER READER WANTS AC#3 STRICTER than "a real terminal device", the outstanding item is one pty run with agent binaries on PATH so the clack multiselect runs before the migration. That is the whole remainder.

RESOLVED BY quest-cli, 2026-09-17: QUEST CAN KNOW WHICH CAUSE IT HIT. THE DESIGN SHIPPED HERE IS THE CORRECT ALGORITHM, NOT A WORKAROUND -- AND MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED INTO PROSE-READING WHEN QCLI-322 SHIPS. That last clause is the reason this note exists.

WHAT WAS ASKED AND WHAT CAME BACK. This session sent quest-cli the two repros and asked, as a question rather than a defect, whether the default-mode Alias collision refusal could report which cause it hit. Two options were offered: add a structured cause, or document that it is not knowable there. quest-cli DECLINED the second explicitly -- "it would be a comfortable answer that isn't true" -- and answered that Quest can know. Filed as quest-cli QCLI-322 (To Do, PR #163).

THEIR MECHANISM, recorded because it is checkable rather than an assurance: assertAliasesAvailable (quest-cli src/domain/records.ts:106-124) seeds a `seen` map from the destination's occupied ids and aliases, then adds each candidate as it walks. At the throw, the match came either from the seed (a destination claim) or from a previously-added candidate (internal renumbering). It knows which and throws a string retaining neither. Repro A is the clean proof: an EMPTY destination means occupied is necessarily empty, and it still throws -- so that collision can only be candidate-vs-candidate.

MY OWN PROVENANCE FLAG PAID OFF, AND IS WORTH REPEATING. The repros in this task were built and run by an implementer subagent, not by this session; the message to quest-cli said so and asked that anything load-bearing be re-resolved. They rebuilt both from scratch against the same installed binary and reported every clause reproduced exactly. They also checked something this session had not: no commit has touched their records.ts or migration module since the v0.7.1 tag, so for this surface the installed bytes and their dev agree -- checked rather than assumed, given 0.7.1 has named more than one byte-set. A subagent's measurement inside your own session is still a relayed measurement; naming it as such is what got it independently verified instead of inherited.

THE CLAIM THAT DID NOT SURVIVE, AND WHERE IT LIVED. The implementing subagent's hand-back asserted that Quest "genuinely cannot know which case it is either at that point." That is now FALSE. It was never written into this record, into src/tracker-migration.ts, into src/commands/init.ts, or into the docs -- checked by search across all four after the answer arrived, not assumed. The shipped comment describes only what the MESSAGE does ("a human explanation of two possibilities, NOT a machine-readable statement of which one occurred"), which remains exactly true; and the question to quest-cli hedged it as unverified. So the hedge did its job and nothing needs correcting. Recorded anyway, because "the wrong claim never escaped" is only knowable if someone writes down that it was checked.

THE PART THAT CHANGES FUTURE WORK -- read this before touching runWizardBacklogMigration. When QCLI-322 ships, a structured cause field will appear on the default-mode refusal, and the obvious simplification will be to read it and delete the preservation-mode preview call. DO NOT. quest-cli's own argument, which they raised against themselves:

  The seed-vs-candidate discriminator is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT for "preservation would resolve it". Preservation can independently refuse on an unpreservable record (unresolvable parent) or on preserved ids that collide among THEMSELVES. A cause field derived from the discriminator alone would sometimes report preservationWouldResolve: true and then refuse on the retry -- which is the exact failure QCLI-256 was raised to stop, in a new costume.

So the only sound answer computes the preservation outcome rather than inferring it, which is precisely what asking the preview does. quest-cli said they would keep this design even if QCLI-322 ships, and that "ask the system that knows, don't read the prose" is the correct algorithm rather than a workaround. If QCLI-322 lands with a cause field, it may be used to IMPROVE the prompt copy (naming the likely cause before asking), never to REPLACE the preview as the authority on whether the retry can succeed.

ONE COMPLICATION THEY RECORDED RATHER THAN SOLVED, relevant if Lore ever offers multi-family imports: preservation takes --source-family and imports one family per run, so a multi-family source has no single answer to "would preservation resolve it". Answering for the colliding record's family, or reporting per family, is a design call on their side -- not unknowability.

CROSS-REFERENCE: quest-cli QCLI-322 (their PR #163). The acceptance example this session proposed went into that task as written and attributed, adding keys under the existing `input` object rather than a new top-level key, so their contractVersion and principal-ordering constraints are untouched. Nothing here asks Lore to change what it shipped.
finalSummary: The wizard's migrate path now runs Quest's preview first and, on an id-collision refusal, offers a retry with --preserve-source-ids/--source-family (family pre-filled from the quoted id, overtypable) instead of dying on a bare exit 5. The design turns on a measured finding: quest 0.7.1's DEFAULT-mode refusal does not say which of the two causes it hit -- it describes both, in prose, with no structured input, and two purpose-built repros returned the same sentence differing only in the quoted id. So Lore classifies nothing from that message. It asks, then lets Quest's own preservation-mode PREVIEW -- which mutates nothing -- be the authority: a plan means positional renumbering and the migration proceeds in the same run; a preservation refusal means a genuine dual claim, which is reported as needing manual resolution rather than retried again. Declining re-raises Quest's refusal verbatim at the same exit 5 the flag path gives. The retry is offered only when no reviewed digest has been recorded, since a resumed migration re-applies that digest and changing options against it could only fail more confusingly. Delivered in PR #137, proven by CI run 35168977253 on head 383af297 (all five require-ci-on-dev contexts green). Three mutants each reddened exactly the predicted subset (3, 4 and 3 cases), so the tests assert the behaviour rather than the implementation's identity. Versions the proofs resolved: lore 0.7.0, quest 0.7.1, backlog 1.50.1, bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0. AC#3's real-terminal proof is a pty with real binaries; its one uncovered combination (clack multiselect before the migration) is recorded on this task rather than left implicit.
